notes: Lowe's Home Decor (lowes.com/c/Home-decor). ACCESS: standard /pl/ and /c/ paths are Akamai-blocked via curl_cffi and Playwright this session (see bs70.json notes). No Clearance-specific sitemap exists (sitemap.xml lists bestsellers0/newreleases0/toprated0.xml but nothing for clearance/outlet), and no Clearance link appears in navigation0.xml or the site's editorial /l/ landing pages (checked landing.xml's full 318-URL list; only found generic dated/event promo pages under /l/savings/* -- black-friday-deals, cyber-deals, daily-deals, labor-day-deals, memorial-day-deals, fourth-of-july-deals, mylowes-rewards-member-deals -- all temporary campaign pages, correctly excluded as Sale not Clearance). A promising sitemap hit, https://www.lowes.com/ple/theoutlet, was opened and confirmed to be a false positive: title 'Theoutlet at Lowes.com' -- 'Theoutlet' is a third-party vendor BRAND name (like the site's other /ple/ brand pages: ideal-air, ideal-security, ideal-decor), not Lowe's own outlet/clearance concept. Guessed URL patterns reusing the working helix-app route family (/clearance/home-decor/..., /special-buys/home-decor/..., /outlet/home-decor/..., /deals/home-decor/...) all returned raw unrendered ESI-template 500 errors -- confirmed these are not registered routes, just a generic error shell. Given /pl/ and /c/ are Akamai-blocked (confirmed again via a Playwright fetch of the one real candidate URL found by web search, https://www.lowes.com/pl/Clearance-items/4294684028 -- also 403/Access-Denied), escalated to Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3, last resort) for this single URL: the real browser loaded it with NO interactive challenge or CAPTCHA to solve (Akamai's JS check passed silently, nothing was 'bypassed' by me) and it auto-redirected to https://www.lowes.com/pl/Deals/1611079983848 ('Deals' page, 15,289 results sitewide) -- confirming the old 'Clearance-items' node no longer exists and has been superseded. That Deals page's own 'Special Offers' facet only offers On Sale / Instant Savings / Buy More Save More / Gift with Purchase / Bulk Savings -- no Clearance value, and no clearance/outlet/final-sale wording anywhere -- so 'Deals' itself was correctly excluded as a generic Sale hub, not Clearance. FOUND THE GENUINE CLEARANCE PAGE via the site's own /l/savings hub: it lists a 'Deals by Category' block whose 'Clearance' link (own link text "Clearance", href /pl/The-back-aisle/2021454685607?refinement=2&int_cmp=...Savings_Page_Lowes_Clearance -- the int_cmp param itself literally names it 'Lowes_Clearance') lands on a real PLP the site brands 'The Back Aisle' (breadcrumb/page-title 'The Back Aisle'), tagged with the on-page copy 'Deals too good to last' -- a clearance/permanent-markdown signal, not a dated campaign, satisfying Sec 3's genuine-taxonomy test. QTY / SCOPE DECISION: the entry link pre-applies a 'Special Offers: On Sale' facet (refinement=2); filtering The Back Aisle to the Home Decor department (catalog=4294935484, same id used throughout) under that facet gives only 9 results (verified by reading the full rendered product list, single page). Removing that facet and viewing the bare, unfiltered The Back Aisle > Home Decor department (https://www.lowes.com/pl/The-back-aisle/2021454685607?catalog=4294935484) gives 247 results (rendered header), with pagination showing 11 pages -- consistent with ~24/page (240 across 10 full pages + 7 on page 11 = 247), not the kind of pagination-contradicting bad count the prior Home-Decor pass flagged elsewhere on this site. I judged the UNFILTERED 247 to be the correct qty: 'On Sale' is only one of several optional Special-Offers sub-filters (Instant Savings, Buy More Save More, Bulk Savings also exist as siblings) available once inside The Back Aisle, not a redefinition of what belongs in the clearance catalog itself -- products land in The Back Aisle by being genuine outlet/clearance stock, and the On-Sale facet the entry link happened to pre-apply looks like a leftover campaign default rather than the concept's own boundary. The left-nav facet's own displayed count for 'Home Decor' (21) was checked and found to disagree with both numbers above (neither 9 nor 247) -- confirming, consistent with this site's known unreliable-facet-count pattern (notes/70.md), that facet counters here should never be trusted over the actual rendered listing, which is what was used.
